💬 Iranian diplomat responds to Netanyahu’s remarks at UN General Assembly

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The third counsellor at the permanent mission of the Islamic Republic of Iran to the United Nations, Nasser Asadi, has responded to the remarks of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu at the UN General Assembly (UNGA) meeting.

In remarks on Thursday at the third day of the UN General Assembly’s general debate, Asadi said, “Mr. President, this organization was founded to save succeeding generations from the scourge of war. Yet today, the chief architect of that very scourge, the notorious Prime Minister of the Israeli regime, addressed this Assembly, an utmost disgrace to this body. This is the ultimate insult to all noble values such as justice, equality, and dignity and worth of the human person enshrined in this Organization’s Charter.”
​
He added, “This is the greatest affront to the principles of humanity and the human conscience. This is a profound betrayal of the purpose and principles of this Organization. The UN was founded to preserve peace and uphold justice, not to serve as a platform for war criminals.”
​
“How can a person who is currently facing proceedings before two international courts for war crimes, crimes against humanity, and genocide be allowed to be present in this Assembly? Does he belong at this podium to justify his crimes, or in the dock of a court of law to answer for genocide?” he said.
​
He emphasized, “According to an assessment by the UN itself, in less than two years, the Israeli regime dropped more than 200,000 tons of explosives on Gaza, equivalent to the total energy of approximately 13 Hiroshima-type nuclear bombs. Just imagine. Today, the regime’s prime minister told this Assembly that he has brutally killed nearly 75,000 Palestinian civilians, mostly women and children, and injured around 157,000 others, simply because he had no other choice. He also added that he made very easily the decision to commit these crimes and crimes like collective punishment, ethnic cleansing, and the use of starvation as a method of war. These data are not Iranian claims. These are judicial findings and documented international legal investigations.”
​
“In January 2024, the ICJ, and in September 2025, the UN Commission of Inquiry concluded that the Israeli regime is committing genocide in Gaza. How can the UN provide a platform to such a notorious criminal? What message does this assembly send to Palestinians when their leaders are barred from speaking here due to the United States’ obstruction, while a criminal responsible for the killing of 75,000 Palestinians is given this podium? If this Assembly barred apartheid South Africa in 1917, why should it grant speaking privileges to this criminal today? Beyond that, why does this Assembly not invoke Article 6 of the Charter of the United Nations to expel this regime from the organization for persistently violating the UN’s principles? Allowing the presence of a criminal at this Assembly fundamentally contradicts the UN’s purpose and principles, which are neither aspirational slogans nor selectively applicable only to some of its members.”
​
“These binding principles, which form the foundation of the international legal order, have been deliberately, persistently, systematically, and systematically violated by the Israeli regime. Its prime minister commits genocide while claiming victimhood, a stark example of hypocrisy. It is a reminder of how they try to present their military as the most moral army in the world.
​
For him [Netanyahu], this is completely natural, as hypocrisy, victim playing, distortion . . .
